passages.quote:
This guidance explains how to complete the questions in the Save As You Earn (SAYE) Employment Related Securities (ERS) annual end of year return. It also identifies which questions are mandatory, conditional mandatory or optional.

There have been some changes made to the end of year return headings. If you wish to create your own end of year template, you can check: (From April 2027) Save As You Earn: technical note.

The current SAYE end of year return is version 7.

1. Who must submit an end of year return

The company secretary, or the person acting as company secretary, must submit an online end of year SAYE ERS end of year return by 6 July following the end of the tax year.

In circumstances where the employee is employed by an Employer of Record (EoR), the EoR is responsible for submitting the returns.

An end of year return must be submitted for each registered and self-certified SAYE scheme.

2. When to submit an end of year return or a nil return

If you operate an ERS scheme, you are required to submit an end of year ERS return, including nil returns, for every scheme registered.

If your scheme has ended and you have entered a final event date, you must submit any outstanding returns up until the date that it ended.

3. Completing and uploading your end of year return

You can use the Employment related securities (ERS) checking service to check your end of year return.

The service:

shows where formatting errors occur which will prevent your end of year return being submitted successfully

can be used as often as needed

helps you correct errors early, making submission easier

You can also access the checking service through ‘View my schemes and arrangements’ on the online ERS service.

4. General guidance on valuations

All values must be entered in pounds sterling to 4 decimal places.

Where necessary:

round up figures ending in 5 or more

round down figures ending in 4 or less

If a value is quoted in another currency, use a reputable currency converter to convert it to pounds sterling.

You do not need to formally agree valuations of shares and securities with HMRC.

Where shares are not listed on a recognised stock exchange, you may have asked HMRC for a valuation. If a valuation was agreed with HMRC:

enter the valuation reference number on the end of year return

if the reference is prefixed with Company Reference Number (CRN), do not enter those letters

If no valuation was agreed, you must retain records showing how the valuation was reasonably determined.

4.1 Actual Market Value (AMV)

AMV is the value of a share or security after taking account of:

restrictions

risk of forfeiture

4.2 Unrestricted Market Value (UMV)

UMV is the value of a share or security ignoring:

restrictions

risk of forfeiture

4.3 Recognised stock exchanges

For more information about recognised stock exchanges read Recognised stock exchanges: definition, legislation and tables.

AIM (Alternative Investment Market) and PISCES (Private Intermittent Securities and Capital Exchange System) are not recognised stock exchanges for these purposes.

5. General guidance on completing the end of year return

5.1 Mandatory, conditional mandatory, and optional fields

Mandatory — a response is always required regardless of any other information provided.

Conditional Mandatory — a response is only required if you have provided a response to a mandatory question.

For example, on the SAYE end of year template where it asks if the shares are listed on a recognised stock exchange, where the answer is ‘no’, the next question will require a response.

Optional — this field can be left blank but should be completed if you know the information requested.

If a conditional mandatory, or optional field does not require a response, leave it blank.

Do not enter:

‘N/A’

‘not applicable’

Doing so will cause your end of year return to be rejected.

5.2 Yes and no answers

The following formats are accepted:

Yes, yes, YES

No, no, NO

6. Common worksheet fields

The following fields appear on most SAYE worksheets. Please refer to this section when completing the common field questions.

6.1 Employee first name

This is the employee’s first name.

This field is mandatory.

6.2 Employee second name (optional).

If the employee has a second name, then enter in this column.

This field is optional.

6.3 Employee last name

This is the employee’s last name.

This field is mandatory.

6.4 National Insurance number

Enter in the correct format, for example, QQ123456C .

Most individuals included on an ERS end of year return will have a National Insurance number.

In exceptional cases, use an alternative reference instead.

This reference must:

only be used on the ERS end of year return

not be used in any other HMRC correspondence

not be given to the individual

Where there are exceptional circumstances, the required format for the alternative ERS reference will be a total of 9 characters. This will be 2 letters, 6 numbers and one letter consisting of:

TN – to indicate an ERS reference

Employee Date of Birth in format DDMMYY (for example, 080403) ― this data will enable HMRC to trace the individual

No National Insurance number Reason Identifier (X, Y or Z) ― this is to identify the reason why an individual does not have a National Insurance number

X ― Under 16 years old

Y ― Applied for a National Insurance number and is waiting to receive it

Z — Never paid National Insurance contributions as they have not been liable to UK National Insurance contributions ― for example, they’re not resident in the UK or are an ‘intra-company worker’ on transfer to work in the UK

This field is mandatory.

7. Worksheet specific guidance

The following sections explain when to use each worksheet and how to complete its questions.

Use a separate row for each individual unless stated otherwise.
